name: Eye whitening and brightening

lead: Eye whitening and brightening is about making the sclera (the white of the eye) look whiter and less red so the eyes look fresher and higher in contrast. Users on looksmax.org argue that white, bright sclera matters for every eye colour because of contrast, and especially for brown eyes.
The idea is that a clearer white sets off the iris more strongly. No studies reviewed examine cosmetic eye whitening or its effect on perceived attractiveness, and the sources found are thin.

paras: Posters ask about eye drops and ways to reduce redness. Whiter-looking eyes are also commonly linked in discussion to everyday factors like sleep and irritation, which people try to manage.

Wikipedia notes alpha agonist drops used for glaucoma have a higher likelihood of allergic reaction, with burning, stinging and other side effects listed; its eye-drop article does not cover redness-relieving drops in depth. Persistent redness is commonly a reason for medical review.

angle.text: Looksmax.org posters argue that whiter, clearer sclera makes the iris stand out more and the eyes look brighter, especially for brown eyes, and ask about eye drops. Little research targets this goal.

lead: Eye whitening and brightening covers the ways people try to make the sclera, the white of the eye, look whiter and less red so the eyes appear clearer, more contrasted and fresher. Looksmaxxing users describe it as a quick contrast adjustment: a whiter sclera makes the iris look more saturated and the area around the eyes look cleaner.[1][2]

The methods discussed in forums are mostly everyday ones. One looksmax.org poster lists a redness-relieving drop (Lumify) as his quickest option, with sleep, hydration and screen breaks as longer-term contributors, and pairs sclera brightness with whiter teeth as a contrast pair.[1] Another poster says sclera whiteness matters for every eye colour and especially for brown eyes, and mentions eye drops.[2] Lumify is a brand of brimonidine, an alpha-2 agonist that is also used in glaucoma drops and a rosacea gel.[3]

Scientific work on the white sclera concerns its role in human gaze signalling and social perception rather than cosmetic whitening: researchers have studied why humans have a uniformly white sclera and how children respond to faces with white versus dark sclera.[4][5] No study has tested cosmetic eye whitening for attractiveness.

paras: The sclera is the white outer layer of the eye. Looksmaxxing posts describe a dull, grey or red sclera as reducing the contrast of the eye area, and a white, clear sclera as making the iris look more saturated and the gaze more energetic.[1] Some posters also say it can help a face look good in photos, and that bright eyes matter more for people with brown eyes.[2]

In one looksmax.org thread the original poster names a brimonidine-based redness drop as the easiest option and says eyes look clearer in the minutes after applying it; he also lists sleep, hydration, regular blinking and breaks from screens as contributors to a brighter sclera.[1] Another poster says he uses eye drops and asks for other suggestions; replies discuss eyeliner or makeup at the lateral canthus and its effect on perceived eye shape.[2]

Brimonidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist: as drops it lowers pressure in open-angle glaucoma, as a gel it treats facial redness in rosacea, and it is also used to reduce redness of the eye. Wikipedia lists itchiness, redness and dry mouth among common eye-drop side effects, and allergic reaction among more serious ones.[3] The general eye-drop article notes that drops carry a lower risk of side effects than oral medicines and that redness lasting more than three days on lubricant drops is a reason to seek medical advice.[6]

Researchers in cognitive science propose that the exposed, uniformly white human sclera evolved to make eye-gaze easier for others to read, and a 2023 review in Trends in Cognitive Sciences updates that hypothesis.[4] A separate 2023 paper reported white sclera in chimpanzees and other mammals, and a 2022 study examined how conspicuous chimpanzee gaze is at realistic distances.[7][8] In a 2023 study, five-year-old children rated faces with white sclera as more cooperative than faces with dark sclera.[5] These studies address eye morphology and social perception, not cosmetic whitening.
No studies found of eye whitening or brightening for appearance. Related research on the evolution and social perception of the white sclera is described above.[4][5]

lore.intro: The topic appears in looksmax.org threads about eye contrast, where sclera whiteness is paired with other contrast features such as teeth.[1][2]
